Contrast agents are known to increase the risk of radiocontrast-induced nephropathy (CIN), particularly in elderly, diabetic, or dehydrated patients. However, the exact molecular mechanisms leading to renal injury in CIN remain unclear. Nicotinamide ameliorates podocyte injury and albuminuria in adriamycin-induced nephropathy. Podocytes are key components of the glomerular filtration barrier, and their injury leads to proteinuria, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and nephrotic syndrome. Effective treatments for these conditions are not well established, and prevention of podocyte injury is a crucial challenge.
